issue_context.title: Add the ability to target an IngressClass controller in a specific namespace
issue_context.body:
**What would you like to be added**:
Modify IngressClass to use ObjectReference instead of TypedLocalObjectReference.

**Why is this needed**:
Ingress controllers are workloads deployed on a cluster inside a namespace. When using multiple ingress controllers in a cluster, using the ObjectReference allows for better integration with those clusters, by having the means to target an ingress controller in a specific namespace.

**API changes**:
```yaml
apiVersion: "networking.k8s.io/v1"
kind: "IngressClass"
metadata:
  name: "external-lb"
spec:
  controller: "example.com/ingress-controller"
  parameters:
    apiGroup: "k8s.example.com/v1alpha"
    kind: "IngressParameters"
    name: "external-lb"
```
would become:
```yaml
apiVersion: "networking.k8s.io/v1"
kind: "IngressClass"
metadata:
  name: "external-lb"
spec:
  controller: "example.com/ingress-controller"
  parameters:
    apiVersion: "k8s.example.com/v1alpha"
    kind: "IngressParameters"
    name: "external-lb"
    namespace: "example-ns"
```
still allowing for users to refer to non-namespaced objects, but adding the ability to refer to objects within a namespace like Istio Gateways.

/sig network
/sig api-machinery

link: istio/istio#27326
comments: I am bit confused on the intent.  IngressClass would still be a non-namespaced object (aside: we need a better word for that, I hereby decree that "rooted" is the opposite of "namespaced" :).  If I have the ability to create a rooted Class object, why do I need to reference a namespaced params?  Clearly I have the authority to create/edit rooted objects?

Because the implementation and its already existing parameters would not (always) be rooted. The intent is to pass the Gateway object as the parameter object here to have Istio automatically configure a route on that specific Gateway when using that IngressClass.

Besides that I can imagine some ingress controllers simply using a ConfigMap as the parameters object here.

Edit: the way it's implemented now basically forces implementers to use rooted custom resources if I understand correctly?

So you want an IngressClass whose params block is an Istio Gateway, am I
getting it right?  Interesting.   Would it make sense to add an
intermediate resource which is not namespaced, which itself contains the
reference to the namespaced Gateway?

On Thu, Jan 7, 2021 at 11:53 PM Yordi Pauptit <notifications@github.com>
wrote:

> Because the implementation and it's already existing parameters would not
> (always) be rooted. The intent is to pass the Gateway object as the
> parameter object here to have Istio automatically configure an IngressClass.
>
> Besides that I can imagine some ingress controllers simply using a
> ConfigMap as the parameters object here.
>
> —
> You are receiving this because you were assigned.
> Reply to this email directly, view it on GitHub
> <https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/97396#issuecomment-756607857>,
> or unsubscribe
> <https://github.com/notifications/unsubscribe-auth/ABKWAVGEIDCUZN5RHGENY2DSY22Y7ANCNFSM4VBYYSTQ>
> .
>

Correct. An intermediate non-rooted resource would be possible, but I personally don't see the benefit of doing this in comparison to switching to `ObjectReference`. I could be missing something here.

As it is now, what kind of object is intented to be used as `parameters` here? As far as I can see it will always be a custom resource created by the implementer of the `IngressClass`, so why not give them the flexibility of using rooted objects?

But again, I might be missing some details here.

/triage accepted

Discussion in sig-net seems to point to this being useful for Gateway, too.  We want consistency between Ingress and Gateway, so I'll accept this.

This warrants a short KEP, I think.

Furthermore, `scheme.AddTypeDefaultingFunc()` requires a type which implements `runtime.Object`.

I added the tag here as well as in `k8s.io/api/networking/*`. Let me know if we only need this in pkg/apis.
